answers.brief_reasoning: Loop: add n%10 to the sum, then divide n by 10 until n is 0. When n is 0 the loop never runs, so it returns 0.
answers.final_answer: public static int digitSum(int n) { int sum = 0; while (n > 0) { sum += n % 10; n /= 10; } return sum; }

answers.brief_reasoning: Start at start and go up by 1 until the number is divisible by its digit sum. For n >= 1 the digit sum is at least 1, so there is no division by zero. The loop always ends because Harshad numbers keep appearing (every power of 10 is one). Check: 11 has digit sum 2 and 11%2 != 0; 12 has digit sum 3 and 12%3 == 0, so the method returns 12.
answers.final_answer: public static int firstHarshad(int start) { int n = start; while (n % digitSum(n) != 0) { n++; } return n; }
